A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Universal Algorithm-Implicit Learning and the same TAIL method. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, cross-modal transfer, label-space extrapolation, computational measurements, and component ablations in Section 6 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds audio classification and evaluation with a substituted image encoder, including per-dataset appendix results.

M1.justification: TAIL retains the same random feature projections, random-injection label dictionary, non-causal transformer, query processing, and training objective. The audio and ResNet-18 experiments use its existing interchangeable-encoder design without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds GTZAN music-genre classification, extending evaluation to an additional unseen modality: audio (Section 6.2, Table 4). This materially broadens the cross-modal test coverage. Existing image datasets, IMDB, and meta-training datasets are retained.

E2.justification: Existing image comparisons retain Linear Probe, ProtoHead, SNAIL, GPICL, and CAML; the text comparison retains Linear Probe, ProtoHead, and GPICL. Audio uses that same cross-modal comparator set. The new ResNet-18 study uses existing Linear Probe and ProtoHead baselines without replacing the original comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds a controlled evaluation that replaces ViT-H with ImageNet-1k-pretrained ResNet-18 only at test time while retaining ViT-H meta-training. Audio evaluation uses wav2vec 2.0 features. These extend the settings; existing episodic sampling, accuracy metrics, and training procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.2 and new Appendix B.2 add a substantive encoder-dependence analysis across four in-domain and nine cross-domain datasets. It tests whether TAIL transfers when its feature extractor changes substantially. The earlier projection, causal-mask, mixed-modality, embedding-schedule, and label-extrapolation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean accuracy and 95% confidence intervals over 1000 sampled test episodes. Added results follow this practice; no new seed reporting, independent training-run counts, significance-testing procedures, or uncertainty-estimation methods are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds audio accuracies: TAIL achieves 55.33%/40.63% in 5-shot/1-shot evaluation, versus ProtoHead's 54.74%/39.09%. New Tables 5–7 report aggregate and per-dataset ResNet-18 results. These are results under new settings; existing image/text scores, ablation values, and plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Appendix A propositions, theorems, assumptions, and proofs retain their substance. Section 3.3 adds learning-curve explanation and citations, while Definition 3.4 corrects the algorithm symbol from a to A; neither changes the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion extend the demonstrated transfer claim from text to text and audio. The introduction and conclusion explicitly delimit the current method to classification. The theoretical framework, three technical contributions, extrapolation claim, and efficiency claim remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the encoder-swap results as showing independence from a specific encoder and greater algorithmic contribution with weaker representations. Section 7 newly acknowledges continued benefits from strong pretrained features and explicitly distinguishes classification-limited TAIL from the task-type-agnostic theoretical framework.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address, identifies wav2vec 2.0 for audio, and specifies ResNet-18's ImageNet-1k pretraining and test-only substitution. It also makes frozen-encoder usage explicit. Architecture hyperparameters, GPICL modifications, and Appendix E optimization details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Schuurmans (1997) and Viering and Loog (2023) for learning curves, Tzanetakis and Cook (2002) for GTZAN, and Baevski et al. (2020) for wav2vec 2.0. Section 5 additionally characterizes discussed foundation-model adaptation methods as typically restricted to one modality; the broader positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized explanatory additions, revised experimental discussion, updated affiliations, a conflict-of-interest disclosure, and small wording and capitalization corrections. Appendix B becomes Additional Results with two subsections. The main section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains grouped text/audio columns, and new Tables 5–7 display ResNet-18 results. Earlier Tables 5–8 become Tables 8–11. Figures and surrounding text are repositioned, but Figures 1–4 retain their content and the document's overall visual format is preserved.

improvement.justification: The audio benchmark and encoder-swap analysis strengthen empirical support for transfer, while explicit applicability limits and code-access information improve transparency. The gain is qualified by an overgeneralized interpretation: Tables 2, 3, and 5 show that the weaker encoder enlarges TAIL's average margins over Linear Probe but reduces them over ProtoHead. The additions provide useful evidence without fully supporting the stronger encoder-dependence conclusion.
